checks: For positive continuous density the increasing quantile and inverse are locally bi-Lipschitz in the interiors. Differentiating W=f(Q)^(p+1) gives W'=(p+1)(f^p)'∘Q/p almost everywhere, and the inverse argument gives the reverse implication. Local absolute continuity and the nonincreasing derivative characterize concavity.

For the convex-combined quantile the rank transform is a negative power mean of the two rank transforms. The Hessian factors as the stated nonpositive scalar times a rank-one positive semidefinite matrix, verified symbolically, and the coordinate derivatives are nonnegative. Concavity passes through this increasing concave map.

The predecessor supplies an actual midpoint in the Minkowski sum and a common first-coordinate rank for the chosen projection. Interior section volumes are positive and their 1/(d−1) roots are concave by Brunn–Minkowski. The d=1 case has affine quantiles of uniform intervals.

The cap-root argument takes inverses only on the closed projected support, including null maximum caps. The inverse of a decreasing concave bijection is decreasing concave. Averaging these inverse tail roots and then inverting yields the midpoint roots. The reflection uses the same comonotone pair with rank reversed.

Jensen with rank-density d r^(d−1) gives the mean threshold at or below upper quantile (d/(d+1))^d and the reflected estimate gives the lower side. The common vector mean follows from the two marginals. No common full-dimensional law across different chosen axes is inferred.
Source §§1, 2, 5 separately establish the direction-specific support, tail shape and stronger density power result.

dependencies.hypotheses: Choose u/||u|| first, t=1/2 and containing convex body (A+B)/2. The proof transports the normalized endpoint volumes and has first coordinate exactly their monotone quantile transport, so their average is the midpoint projection quantile.

overlap.comparison: The accepted proof constructs the needed direction-first transport and bounds the full midpoint density by a constant. It does not assert concavity of positive density powers under arbitrary one-dimensional quantile interpolation.
The accepted multiway theorem supplies an interpolated measure with bounded density and a centroid, with no shape of scalar marginals or both tails for a specified common rank.

readability: The statement and proof scopes agree.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The rank-coordinate argument proves density-power concavity under scalar quantile interpolation, and its directional midpoint and centroid-tail consequences stay on the proper projection domain.
